Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** A Beijing brain surgeon let ChatGPT grind for 16 hours and walked away with a proof mathematicians had chased since 2004. OpenAI claimed a Cold War uranium site for its next data center. China's GLM-5.3 dug up a software bug planted in 1981, and Higgsfield quadrupled its value in seven months.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **ChatGPT:** How did a brain surgeon end a 22-year math hunt in one run?

* **OpenAI:** What is it building where America enriched uranium?

* **Z.ai:** How old is the oldest bug its model just dug up?

* **Higgsfield:** What convinced Goldman to back a 4x jump in seven months?


----------



----------
## A brain surgeon beat 22 years of math with ChatGPT

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/39e3de36-d496-412f-9e69-29bd8ba57b10/math_1.png?t=1786997094)
Caption: 

Jin Shanmu is a neurosurgery resident in Beijing. His degree is in geology and every bit of math past the basics is self-taught, picked up for his research on brain ultrasounds.

Last month he proved [Crouzeix's conjecture](https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3363966/chinese-doctor-stuns-maths-world-cracking-decades-old-problem-using-chatgpt), a matrix problem that had stumped mathematicians since 2004.

His method was a 16-hour autonomous run of GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT Work. He cut the model off from the internet, told it to split into subagents that chase different strategies and audit each other's proofs, then walked away.

The proof survived. Michel Crouzeix, who posed the problem, [checked it himself](https://alextownsend.net/essays/SIAMNews_CrouzeixConjecture.pdf) and believes it's correct, with formal peer review still pending. The exact prompt sits on GitHub, adapted from one OpenAI used on another open conjecture.

Eight days later two mathematicians posted an independent proof. They disclosed using ChatGPT too.

ChatGPT keeps making math history every other month. Can’t wait for it to make breakthroughs in biology as well.

77598.body:
The Data and Insights newsletter brings the highlights of the week from The Block’s Data Dashboard

( https://www.theblock.co/data/crypto-markets/spot )

Presented by:

Bitget ( https://www.bitget.com/campaigns/project-archimedes?channelCode=regd&vipCode=bw1d )

Gm data enjoyers! We are halfway through August and hope everyone's been enjoying some time in the sun! With trillions of dollars of real-world assets migrating onto blockchain rails we are introducing a way for readers to keep up to date with market insights and visual analyses on what matters in the world of Tokenization. Sign up here ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters ). Our first issue releases soon!

This week, we’re taking a look at onchain equities and STRC stock. We’ll also look at prediction market fundraising, exchange volume, and Robinhood Chain’s continued growth. So grab a drink, take a seat, and let's dive in.

1: Cambrian Stock Explosion

( https://www.theblock.co/data/decentralized-finance/real-world-assets/rwa-market-cap-by-asset-class-market-share )

Chart via The Block's Data Dashboard

*Key Insights* provided by The Block Research

* Tokenized stock market share has grown to 15%, up 3x from the start of the year. It’s been one of the few RWA categories to see growth as interest in onchain equity trading has ballooned. Total market cap sits around 2.8 billion at the time of writing.

* RWA transfer volume has also rocketed, doubling in August to $20 billion, up from $9 billion the month prior.
* Despite accounting for a relatively small share of the total RWA market, tokenized equities have drawn the most attention from retail investors and have become an entry point to onchain applications.

* Three contenders have emerged in the race to bring stocks onchain. Ondo Finance, Binance (bStock), and xStocks have captured the majority of market share, collectively accounting for an impressive 77%. Ondo sits with the largest slice at $957 million while bStocks and xStocks command $622 and $600 million, respectively.

* All 3 leverage synthetic representations of underlying stock. While the specific mechanics vary, each aims to replicate the actual stock performance while giving the investor a derivative to transact or trade.
* Other builders such as Securitize and Superstate are working to bring actual equity onchain, where shares issued on the blockchain carry the same rights as conventional shares.

* Tokenized equity companies are choosing between first-to-distribute and onchain native tokenization. While synthetic stocks are being traded more frequently, they lack the full ownership, governance, and shareholder protections of the underlying asset.

How are global and regional ETF markets performing?        Discover how the rise of real-time payments is reshaping cash flow for businesses.  Want more content from In Context? Sign up here to receive weekly insights directly in your inbox. The AI infrastructure buildout is fueling “chipflation” AI data center demand is creating a shortage of global memory capacity, with prices for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) estimated to rise more than 400% from the start of 2024 to the end of 2026, according to J.P. Morgan Global Research. For the average consumer, implications of the memory shortage may already be felt in the form of “chipflation,” or inflation of the cost of memory for chips in common electronics — from phones and computers to smartwatches and TVs. 77592.subject: Hyperliquid’s Spot Wars
77592.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

BTC continues to struggle while gold regains momentum. Bitcoin fell 3.1% last week even as equities and gold moved higher, with softer inflation data reducing expectations for another Fed hike. 

Meanwhile, Hyperliquid has found its next battleground. After HIP-3 drove its expansion into RWA perps, xStocks, EQX and Dinari are now competing to build out tokenized equities on spot. We look at whether the market can finally gain traction, alongside compute futures and tokenization’s shift from access to utility.

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

BTC once again looked weak last week, falling 3.1% while every other major benchmark ended higher. The Nasdaq led with a 1.4% gain, followed by gold at 0.8% and the S&P 500 at 0.5%.

Gold had a stellar start to the year, with YTD gains peaking at 30% toward the end of January. It then spent much of the year giving those returns back, falling from around $5.6K per ounce to $4K. Over the past month, however, gold has started to look strong again, gaining 10.7% and comfortably outperforming the other major benchmarks.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/38fda02b-b76d-4895-8218-3d46d85cd453/image.png?t=1786967450)
Caption: 

Softer inflation data last week [reduced](https://www.reuters.com/business/gold-gains-weaker-dollar-reduced-fed-rate-hike-bets-2026-08-17/) expectations that the Fed will raise interest rates next month, with the odds falling from 47% a month ago to 30% today. At the same time, central banks have continued to buy gold at record levels. According to the World Gold Council, net purchases between April and June were more than [five](https://www.reuters.com/commentary/reuters-open-interest/central-banks-spearhead-renewed-gold-rush-2026-08-13/) times higher than during the previous three months.

While gold and BTC are both seen as hedges against inflation and dollar debasement, the same momentum has yet to reach Bitcoin. BTC remains stuck between $62K and $64K, while weekly ETF flows continue to flip between inflows and outflows. Funds recorded $159M of net outflows last week.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f4537cce-a403-4f43-96ee-cf6a902e10c4/image.png?t=1786967449)
Caption: 

Across the different sectors, the Oracle index led the market with a 14.5% gain, followed by L2s at 6.7%.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=sc
